location: lines 734 and 825 (hardware cells 4.1 and 4.2; same pattern in the 4.3 skeleton, line 1000)
issue: `usage_s` is taken from `float(job.usage() or 0.0)` immediately after `job.result()`. In qiskit-ibm-runtime 0.49.0 `BaseRuntimeJob.usage()` returns 0 while the server-side usage record is still `status == 'pending'`, which is routinely the case right after the result arrives. The notebook therefore records `usage_s = 0.0` for real jobs, and `grade_ex4_1` (usage <= 30 s) / `grade_ex4_2` (usage <= 180 s, -5 gate) are then evaluated against 0 — the QPU-budget gates become vacuous and the submitted job_info is wrong.
evidence: site-packages/qiskit_ibm_runtime/base_runtime_job.py:125-150: `if usage.get('status','pending') == 'pending': return 0`; docstring: 'the job usage returned is 0 until the usage calculation is completed'. Confirmed by docs page api/qiskit-ibm-runtime/runtime-job-v2#usage and guides/max-execution-time, which recommends `job.metrics()['usage']['quantum_seconds']` for completed jobs.
fix: After `job.result()`, poll `job.metrics()['usage']` until `status != 'pending'` (bounded retry, e.g. 10 x 6 s) and take `quantum_seconds` (or `job.usage()` once non-zero); if still unavailable, fall back to `USAGE_MODEL(executions)` and set `job_info['usage_estimated'] = True` so the grader/organizer can see it was not measured. Apply the same in the 4.3 skeleton comment.
